subject: [PATCH v3 2/2] zstd: use cpu_feature_enabled() for in-kernel BMI2 dispatch

reviews.author: Usama Arif (author)
reviews.summary:
Author acknowledged a concern about the cached state of BMI2 support and agreed to make a change in the next version.

Author tried to use a different include order, but it broke another file due to naming conflicts; they are unsure about their approach and ask for reassessment.
reviews.raw_body:
Good catch! Thanks. I will change to:

Cached for per-context dispatch: 1 if the CPU supports BMI2, 0 otherwise.

---

I tried that, but compiler.h is included by unrelated zstd translation units.
On x86, <asm/cpufeature.h> eventually includes <asm/current.h>, which defines
current as get_current(). This breaks the existing local variable named current 
in zstd_double_fast.c.

I think the current apporach is ok?

2026-09-03.patch_summary: This patch improves the performance of Zstandard (ZSTD) compression and decompression in the Linux kernel by using CPU feature checks to enable BMI2 instructions at runtime, rather than relying on static CPUID probing. The patch introduces a new abstraction for context initialization and uses x86 feature policy to allow x86 alternatives to resolve feature checks at boot time. This change improves performance by reducing the number of branches and allowing the CPU to optimize instruction sequences. Benchmarks show a 19.5% reduction in compression time and a 72.3% reduction in decompression time.

reviews.author: Nick Terrell
reviews.summary: Reviewer Nick Terrell suggested dropping support for CPUID-backed dispatch in the preboot environment to simplify code and potentially improve performance, noting that this would cost about 10% of performance.
reviews.raw_body:
I don't know a lot about the preboot environment, but should we consider just
dropping support for the CPUID-backed dispatch in the preboot environment?
That would cost about 10% of performance, but perhaps the simplicity
is worth it.
